quote: un test conceptual es decir que N e Int son isomorfismos (o lo que realmente sean) y probarlo con un test.
what: A de novo conceptual implementation of the integers alongside the machine's natural implementation; a conceptual test states that `N` and `Int` are isomorphic (or whatever they really are) and proves it with a test.

quote: la definición conceptual sirve de oráculo para la implementación de la máquina.
what: `N` is not isomorphic to `Int` (which has negatives) but to the non-negative integers `Nat := { k : Int | 0 <= k }`, with the isomorphism respecting sum and product; the conceptual definition serves as oracle for the machine implementation, and the certificate records the range tested. Changing the extern to int64 makes it fail at the `2^63` border.

quote: `check` solo verifica tipos ... y registra que además hay dos leyes que probar, pero no las prueba ... si cambiás una definición o algo de lo que depende, vuelven a `stale` y hay que correr `test` otra vez.
what: `check` only verifies types and registers which laws remain to prove (`pending`); the laws are run by `test`, which also writes the certificate and turns definitions to `certified`, or back to `stale` when a definition or its dependency changes.

quote: no la semilla ni los rangos del generador, así que la corrida no es reproducible desde el certificado. Lo arreglo: cada corrida elige y guarda una semilla, guarda los parámetros de generación y una descripción del dominio de cada variable
what: A certificate that doesn't record the seed, generation parameters and domain of each variable isn't reproducible; each run now chooses and stores a seed, the generation params, a domain description per variable, and sample cases.

quote: El generador de `N` produce números chicos, entre 0 y 4 ... para leyes sobre naturales alcanza para atrapar errores de estructura pero no de magnitud
what: Unary `N` generated by depth only reaches small numbers, enough for structural errors but not magnitude; for laws about magnitude the law is written on `Nat` (ranged `Int`), with `fromInt` to `N`.

quote: es un parámetro escondido, y hoy está registrado en el certificado justamente porque un parámetro escondido que afecta la garantía tiene que estar a la vista.
what: The max depth 4 was a hidden parameter with no criterion; a hidden parameter that affects the guarantee has to be recorded and exposed.

quote: el tamaño es un parámetro del test, y crece con el número de caso. Los primeros casos son chicos, así un contraejemplo sale mínimo y legible; los últimos son grandes, así se cubre magnitud.
what: Following QuickCheck, size is a test parameter (`--depth`) that grows from 1 to the cap along the n cases, so first counterexamples are minimal and legible and later cases cover magnitude; the recursive constructor is chosen with bias 0.8 while depth remains.

quote: ahora quiero ver si estas implementando cosas en python que debieran estar en luthier. por ejemplo float_range o  int_range
what: Luciano asks whether things are being implemented in Python that should be in Luthier, naming `float_range` and `int_range`.

quote: En Python tiene que estar la máquina ... y el puente ... Todo lo que sea una decisión que cambia lo que el certificado significa tiene que estar en Luthier, escrito y visible.
what: Criterion for the split: Python holds the machine (the `int`/`float` ops behind `extern`) and the bridge (converting Luthier values to Python); any decision that changes what the certificate means must be written and visible in Luthier.

open: arithmetic and `test` left as second and third steps, not done.
quote: Un generador es una función, `Gen A := Int -> Int -> A * Int` ... la aritmética: el tipo de `+` no está escrito en ningún lado. Debería ser `addInt : Int -> Int -> Int := extern ...` en el preludio ... El propio `test`, que en el diseño es una función sobre `Program` y hoy es Python.
what: Three things wrongly in Python: generators as a type `Gen A := Nat -> Int -> A * Int` with one `size` unifying range and depth; arithmetic as `addInt : Int -> Int -> Int := extern ...` with the operator as sugar; and `test` itself as a function over `Program`, waiting for `Term` to be data.

quote: `genNat` devuelve un `Nat`, así que tiene una ley propia, que el generador nunca produce un negativo, y el preludio pasó a tener una obligación.
what: Because `genNat` returns a `Nat`, it carries its own law (the generator never produces a negative), so the generator library itself acquires an obligation and travels certified.

quote: Es un defecto de distribución, y una ley cuantificada sobre casos individuales nunca lo ve ... hace falta la capa estadística de tus audios de mayo, una ley sobre la muestra y no sobre el caso ... con un veredicto probabilístico. Es el primer caso concreto donde el matrimonio con Bayes deja de ser una frase.
what: A biased generator is a distribution defect no per-case quantified law can see, since each value alone is legitimate; catching it directly needs a law over the sample with a probabilistic verdict, the statistical (Bayes) layer from the May audios.

quote: el primer fallo aparece en el borde del dominio, y eso te dice el rango donde la función sirve.
what: Because size grows during the run, the first failure of `asin (sin x) ≈ x` appears just past `-π/2`, the border of the domain where the law stops holding, which is the information a test should give.

quote: La función no cambió; cambió lo que se afirma de ella, y el certificado dice cuál de las dos afirmaciones es verdad y en qué dominio.
what: The same `sin` declared as inverse of `asin` over all `R` fails, but over the principal branch `{ x : R | -π/2 <= x and x <= π/2 }` passes; the function doesn't change, what changes is what is asserted, and the certificate says which assertion is true and in what domain.

quote: mejor una semilla por corrida de la que se deriva la de cada definición, y `--seed` repite todo.
what: Instead of each definition drawing its own seed, one seed per run from which each definition's is derived, so `--seed` repeats the whole run.

quote: no me gusta prelude. me parece que deberia ser disgregado en sus componentes y que todo vaya a examples quizas? o hay algo fundamental? yo creo que sonolocalization no va a usar nada de esto no?
what: Luciano dislikes the prelude and proposes breaking it into its components, moving everything to examples, and questions whether anything is fundamental and whether sonolocalización will use any of it.

quote: es fundamental solo lo que el intérprete nombra por su cuenta al elaborar ... Eso cabe en veinte líneas. Todo lo demás ... son librerías que se importan a pedido.
what: Fundamental is only what the interpreter names on its own while elaborating (`Bool`, `List` for literals, `Unit`/`Maybe` for the Python bridge, `Nat`); that fits in twenty lines as `core.lut`, everything else (Peano, algebra, generators, reals) is a library imported on demand in `lib/`.

quote: Hace falta un tipo opaco, `Signal : U := extern \"python:numpy.ndarray\"`, cuyos valores pasan por Luthier sin tocarse y solo los `extern` operan sobre ellos.
what: numpy arrays can't enter Luthier as a list of `cons`; an opaque type `Signal : U := extern "python:numpy.ndarray"` lets values pass through Luthier untouched, with only `extern` operating on them.

quote: las leyes se escriban en la sesión de Sonolocalización, que conoce las rutinas y sus firmas, y que Luthier crezca acá cuando allá aparezca algo que no se puede expresar.
what: The laws of a delay estimator should be written in the Sonolocalización session that knows the routines and their signatures and invariants; Luthier grows here when something there can't be expressed.

quote: mas que diez mil, un millon
what: Correcting the scale, the signals are not ten thousand but a million samples.

quote: no tienen `==`, comparar señales es una función a `R` con tolerancia.
what: Opaque signals have no `==`; comparing two signals is a function to `R` with tolerance.

quote: La identidad Cov[g] = ρ/2 del docstring de `gcc` vale solo en los retardos donde el template cae entero dentro de la ventana.
what: A real finding: the Cov[g] = ρ/2 identity in the gcc docstring holds only where the template falls entirely inside the window; where it pokes out, variance drops.

quote: Luthier describe (tipos, leyes, `extern`, `test`) y Python hace el trabajo.
what: The criterion inherited from the Luthier handoff note: Luthier only describes (types, laws, extern, test) and Python does the work.

quote: Yo pienso en conceptos: el mas importante primero. Cual es la certificacion mas importante? cual es la siguiente? que fallo?
what: A rule for how work is reported to him: think in concepts, most important first, name what failed or what limit was hit; a count like "33 laws" tells him nothing.

quote: El límite de Luthier es que no expresa esperanzas ... y no certifica una corrida concreta ni objetos que son archivos, por eso las etapas 00 a 04 son huecos tipados.
what: Sonolocalización's likelihood is certified by Luthier, the field stages are not, and that boundary is Luthier's limit, not sonolik's: Luthier v0 does not express expectations, nor certify a concrete run, nor handle objects that are files.

quote: La verosimilitud está definida en Python, y Luthier solo enuncia leyes sobre ella.
what: The likelihood is defined in Python and Luthier only states laws about it; the model names this as a gap in what it built.

quote: La idea es que luthier es donde se expresan los conceptos, si no definimos ahi la likelihood estamos mal
what: Luthier is the place where the concepts are expressed; if the likelihood is not defined there, the work is misdirected.

quote: La idea es que luthier es donde se expresan los conceptos, si no definimos ahi la likelihood estamos mal
what: Luthier is where concepts are expressed; if the likelihood is not defined there, the design is wrong.

quote: Luthier solo describe: tipos, leyes, extern a Python y test; ninguna función con cuerpo
what: The criterion taken from the hand-off note was that Luthier only describes (types, laws, externs, tests) with no function bodies, which left it as a test harness over the Python modules rather than the home of the concepts.

quote: La unidad de organización fue el módulo de Python (trace, noise, window), no el concepto ... Nunca me pregunté cuáles son los conceptos de sonolocalización y cómo se escriben como tipos.
what: Taking the handoff note literally made Luthier a test harness over sonolik; the unit of organization was the Python module, not the concept, so the likelihood stayed in Python as a black box.

quote: sabes que los tipos incluyen las funciones con las leyes que las rigen no?
what: Types in Luthier include the functions together with the laws that govern them.

quote: sabes que los tipos incluyen las funciones con las leyes que las rigen no?
what: Types include the functions and the laws that govern them.

quote: el concepto central no tiene tipo: no hay un `LogLikelihood` que diga qué leyes cumple una verosimilitud
what: Function subtypes with laws are the concepts (a LawfulCorrelator says what a correlator is), but the central concept, the log-likelihood, has no type of its own, and the laws written mix the defining ones with implementation details of gcc.

quote: el concepto central no tiene tipo: no hay un `LogLikelihood` que diga qué leyes cumple una verosimilitud ... las leyes que escribí mezclan las que definen el concepto con las que describen la implementación de gcc
what: The central concept lacks a type: there is no `LogLikelihood` with its laws; and the written laws mix those that define the concept with those describing gcc's implementation.

quote: que tipos describen los emisores y los receptores de sonido?
what: Starting from the fundamentals, what types describe the emitters and receivers of sound.

quote: Un receptor es una función de la presión en un punto a una grabación, y un emisor es una función del tiempo a un campo de presión.
what: A receiver is a function from pressure at a point to a recording, an emitter a function from time to a pressure field; the types are those functions with the laws that make the likelihood valid.

quote: La inferencia es sobre objetos fisicos del mundo real: emisores y receptores situados en tiempo espacio y frecuencia de emision etc
what: The point is inference, and inference is about real-world physical objects: emitters and receivers situated in time, space, and emission frequency.

quote: La inferencia es sobre objetos fisicos del mundo real: emisores y receptores situados en tiempo espacio y frecuencia de emision etc
what: Inference is over real-world physical objects: emitters and receivers situated in time, space and emission frequency.

quote: Entonces el tipo primario no es la función sino el objeto situado, y la función (grabar, propagar) es el modelo directo que lo conecta con los datos.
what: The primary type is the situated object, not the function; the function (record, propagate) is the forward model, and inference is the inverse path, filling a hole with a value decorated by its uncertainty.

quote: el tipo primario no es la función sino el objeto situado ... La inferencia es el camino inverso: de las grabaciones a las coordenadas del objeto.
what: The primary type is the situated object, not the function; recording/propagating is the forward model, and inference is the inverse path from recordings to the object's coordinates, yielding a value decorated by its uncertainty.

quote: Bueno, es un grafo. Al final llegamos a estos tipos, en el medio inferimos sobre la traza de python, creo.
what: The whole thing is a graph: the physical-object types at the ends, inferring over the Python trace in the middle.

quote: es un grafo. Al final llegamos a estos tipos, en el medio inferimos sobre la traza de python, creo.
what: The structure is a graph; at the ends are the situated-object types, in the middle inference runs over the Python trace.

quote: te parece armara un archivo lut con las definiciones de Emitter, Receiver etc?
what: Build a .lut file with the definitions of Emitter, Receiver, etc.

quote: aca hablamos en castellano, pero todo lo que queda escrito (salvo mis transcriptos obviamente) va en ingles, ponelo en tu memoria.
what: Chat is in Spanish but everything written (except his transcripts) goes in English.

quote: la idea de luthier es que sea acumulativo, es decir no calcular dos veces lo mismo (excepto override command) y que el conocimiento se vaya acumulando en una base de datos relacional quizas?
what: What remains are files and graphics; the human interface is reading comprehensible files (perhaps json); Luthier should be cumulative, never computing the same thing twice (except on override) with knowledge accumulating, perhaps in a relational database.

quote: la idea de luthier es que sea acumulativo, es decir no calcular dos veces lo mismo (excepto override command) y que el conocimiento se vaya acumulando en una base de datos relacional quizas?
what: Luthier should be cumulative: never compute the same thing twice (except an override command), with knowledge accumulating in a relational database.

quote: aca hablamos en castellano, pero todo lo que queda escrito (salvo mis transcriptos obviamente) va en ingles
what: Chat is in Spanish but everything that stays written goes in English, except his transcripts.

what: His way of working: what remains after running scripts are files and pdfs; the human interface is reading comprehensible files, perhaps json.

quote: lo que queda son files, y la pieza que los hace acumulativos ya existe en Luthier, el hash del cono de dependencias de cada definición.
what: The accumulative piece already exists as the hash of each definition's dependency cone; a definition's value can be a file whose hash includes the input data, giving content-addressed build; a relational db serves as a reconstructible index, not the source of truth.

open: Requires Luthier cases 5 and 6 (a type whose value is a file with its hash, and the certificate of an instance over concrete data), still unbuilt.

what: Content-addressed build: a definition's hash depends on function, arguments and input hashes; files are the truth with a small json sidecar, and the relational DB is a reconstructible index, not the source of truth.

quote: dos objetos no pueden ocupar el mismo lugar al mismo tiempo.
what: Absolute GPS/datetime coordinates fix identity (two objects cannot occupy the same place at the same time, matters for certification and hash), but that precision is impractical for the experiment, so both kinds of type must be expressed.

quote: dos objetos no pueden ocupar el mismo lugar al mismo tiempo. Ahora, esta precision no es practica a nivel del experimento. We have to express both kind of types.
what: Position and time can be fixed absolutely (GPS, date-time), which matters for certification/hash since two objects cannot occupy the same place at the same time; but that precision is not practical for the experiment, so both kinds of type are needed.

quote: hay dos sistemas de coordenadas con dos funciones distintas, y el tipo tiene que tener los dos.
what: Two coordinate systems with distinct roles, absolute (identity, hash) and local (inference), joined by a Frame, with a consistency law between them and a law that two objects do not share a local position at the same time.

quote: hay dos sistemas de coordenadas con dos funciones distintas ... Las coordenadas absolutas ... son la identidad ... Las coordenadas locales ... son donde la medición tiene precisión de centímetros y donde corre la inferencia.
what: Two coordinate systems with distinct roles (absolute geodesic = identity and hash; local metres = inference) joined by a Frame, with a consistency law between them and an "apart" law for the scene.

quote: la idea es que sea un functor, es decir que decoremos la posicion con una incerteza.
what: There must be a type for a credibility interval or probability density (a prior over position); the idea is a functor that decorates a value, e.g. position, with an uncertainty.

quote: la idea es que sea un functor, es decir que decoremos la posicion con una incerteza.
what: A type for credibility interval or probability density, able to express a prior over position, as a functor that decorates position with uncertainty.

open: which of the five is canonical was the model's recommendation, not settled by Luciano.

open: Whether `F : U -> U` works as a type parameter in Luthier was not tested.

what: Five ways to decorate a value with uncertainty, distinguished by how exact the functor is and what they lose; Dist over a grid is proposed as canonical, with region and gaussian as derived summaries, and `Emitter (F : U -> U)` to avoid duplicating the type; dependence on the calibration is bind, not map.

quote: La idea es que luthier exprese los conceptos pero la representacion se delegue a Python.
what: Luthier expresses the concepts and the representation is delegated to Python; a question whether lut programs could be compiled to Python and then run.

quote: La idea es que luthier exprese los conceptos pero la representacion se delegue a Python ... si no se podrian compilar los programas de lut a python y luego correr python.
what: Luthier expresses the concepts while representation is delegated to Python; could the .lut programs be compiled to Python and then run?

quote: No es al pedo, pero el motivo no es correr más rápido: es que hoy la representación en Python se escribe a mano, y eso es lo que un compilador tiene que eliminar.
what: Compiling to run gains little; the point is to generate the Python representation that today is written by hand (dataclasses per type, booleans per law, stubs per hole), so objects stop being opaque.

quote: el motivo no es correr más rápido: es que hoy la representación en Python se escribe a mano, y eso es lo que un compilador tiene que eliminar.
what: Compiling to run faster is almost worthless; the value is compiling the declaration to the representation, eliminating the hand-written Python that mirrors the .lut, with the generated .py never edited and carrying the .lut's hash.

quote: Las dos alternativas hacen lo mismo con el `.lut`, lo leen y producen la representación en Python; difieren en cuándo lo hacen y en dónde queda el resultado.
what: Two alternatives to produce the Python representation: compile to files (readable, editor/mypy support, build step) or load the .lut at import (one source of truth, classes only at runtime); both need the same type-to-representation map, and the model would start with loading at import.

quote: el `.lut` solo declara `signalAt : Scene -> Receiver -> Signal` y es `sonolik` quien dice con qué lo llena.
what: Inverting the arrow so the .lut declares the hole with a signature and the environment (sonolik) fills it by registration, instead of signatures coming from what Python already has.

quote: Las dos alternativas hacen lo mismo con el `.lut`, lo leen y producen la representación en Python; difieren en cuándo lo hacen y en dónde queda el resultado.
what: Two ways to produce the Python representation from the .lut: compile to files (A, readable, editor and mypy support, but two artifacts and a build step) or load on import (B, single source of truth, but classes exist only at runtime); B is the engine, A is B plus "print it".

quote: En un punto lo que estamos haciendo es un dsl en python no?

quote: Lo que no es un DSL embebido, y es lo único que justifica un lenguaje aparte, son cuatro cosas.
what: In implementation it is a DSL in Python; only four things justify a separate language (the judgment that a value satisfies a type, the certificate as persistent composable evidence, the hole as a first-class citizen, and environment independence), plus a future fifth of proving rather than testing; these pay only if actually used.

open: These pay only if used (certificates accumulate across projects, a hole filled by more than one environment, the .lut read without Python); otherwise it is "un hypothesis peor".
quote: Lo que no es un DSL embebido, y es lo único que justifica un lenguaje aparte, son cuatro cosas. Primera, el juicio ... Segunda, el certificado como evidencia persistente y componible ... Tercera, el hueco como ciudadano ... Cuarta, la independencia del entorno
what: Four things justify a language apart rather than an embedded DSL: judgment (the obligation is born from the declaration), the certificate as persistent composable evidence, the hole as a citizen the checker knows, and independence from the environment; a fifth, future: v0 tests, the aim is that one day it proves.

quote: El paso uno invierte la flecha.

quote: quizas mejor desarrollamos todo el programa lut para despues hacer la implementacion en python no?
what: Develop the whole .lut program first, then do the Python implementation.

quote: una ley se escriba solo cuando ya sabemos que es verdadera, por la matemática o por los test de pytest existentes
what: A hole-filled program is valid and check verifies its types; a law should be written only when already known true (by math or existing tests), because an unverified law that turns out false is worse than a hole.

quote: una ley se escriba solo cuando ya sabemos que es verdadera, por la matemática o por los test de pytest existentes ... una ley no verificada que después resulta falsa es peor que un hueco.
what: A program full of holes is a valid program whose check verifies the types; the complete .lut is the specification, and a law is written only when already known true (by math or existing pytest), since an unverified law that turns out false is worse than a hole.

what: e.position is correct and is pure syntactic sugar over a match on the pattern the type already declares, needing no new Term constructor, and it resolves the name-collision of root-level projection functions.

quote: y para calificacion de modulo podes usar la notacion C++  z7::addMod7 ?
what: Whether module qualification could use C++ notation z7::addMod7, then whether that is the same thing as projection.

quote: El punto sirve para las dos cosas porque son la misma: un módulo es un registro cuyas componentes son sus definiciones, así que calificar es proyectar.
what: The dot serves both projection and module qualification because they are the same: a module is a record whose components are its definitions, so qualifying is projecting; subtypes with named components became dependent products.

quote: Si vas a tener dos sesiones sobre la misma carpeta, decime cuál es dueña de qué archivos, porque la próxima colisión puede pisar algo sin que ninguna de las dos lo note.

what: The tests for the positioning module are not to be written now; they are to be generated using Luthier.

quote: sirve para verificar que la covarianza de Laplace da bien. Pero eso es tarea de los tests de Luthier, no de la interfaz.
what: Verifying the Laplace covariance on simulated data with a known truth and known σ belongs to Luthier's tests, not to the interface module.

quote: ahora quiero pensar como luthierizar esta funcion MAP . es decir definir sus invariantes y testearlas.
what: Luciano frames "luthierizing" a function (here the MAP) as defining its invariants and testing them.

quote: Estas son las diez invariantes que propongo: 1. **Calibración de la covarianza.** ... 2. **Score nulo en el MAP.** ... 3. **Hessiano exacto.** ...
what: The model proposes ten invariants for the MAP (covariance calibration, null score at the MAP, exact Hessian, rigid motion, scale, permutations, prior limits, σ unbiasedness, noiseless data, multiple starts).

open: whether there is an analogous exact test for the MAP, since MAP samples the posterior only approximately and he cannot tell if it is structurally wrong.
quote: si vos tenes una funcion que samplea de una distribucion y tenes una propuesta de likelihood, vos tenes que el promedio del score tiende a cero y el promedio del hessiano tiende a la varianza del score. Eso tiene la ventaja que se aplica a cualquier problema de likelihood.
what: From his macro_dr work, the relation between a sampler and a proposed likelihood: the mean of the score tends to zero and the mean of the Hessian tends to the variance of the score, applicable to any likelihood problem; he doubts a like equivalence exists for the MAP.

quote: Hay una equivalencia exacta, pero no es para el MAP. Es para la posterior verdadera, y el MAP con su Laplace se testea como aproximación de esa posterior.
what: The model separates three levels: the score identities hold at the true θ for likelihood and prior together; the posterior has an exact Bayesian calibration identity; the MAP with Laplace deviates with a known form that vanishes as σ_d/L → 0, and importance sampling can make the MAP exact.

quote: el MAP es una propiedad local y se puede certificar sin un estándar. Lo que no se puede certificar localmente es la covarianza, y la identidad del score en el MAP hay que formularla por fila.
what: The MAP is a local property certifiable without a standard (null gradient, negative definite Hessian), while the covariance is not; the Bartlett identity must be stated per measurement row, which is White's information matrix test and yields the sandwich covariance.

quote: MAP tiene una invariante que es que las condiciones de terminacion se cumplen, esto es el score es suficientemente chico, o nos excedimos en iters o cosas asi. ... La likelihood por otra parte esta asociada a una funcion espejo de muestreo y ambas se testean mutuamente.
what: The MAP's invariant is that its termination conditions hold (score small enough, or iterations exceeded); testing the termination boolean is not the same as testing each iteration, and the likelihood has a mirror sampling function with which it is tested mutually.

quote: el algoritmo produce un registro y el test es un predicado sobre ese registro, sin reimplementar nada.
what: The MAP is tested with the likelihood as the likelihood is tested with the sampler, forming a closed chain; the iteration's own invariants are checked over an optional trace without reimplementing it, fitting Luthier's logic of a predicate over a record.

quote: tenemos que exponer la funcion MAP...._step y luego aplicar un reduce sobre esta con la predicado is_MAP_finished sobre el step. Y usariamos una funcion reduce general para armar MAP...
what: Expose the MAP step function and apply a reduce over it with the predicate is_MAP_finished, using a general reduce to assemble the MAP.

quote: No es un reduce, es un \"iterar hasta\". ... La forma natural es un driver genérico `iterate_until(step, is_finished, state0)` ... Separar el algoritmo del modelo.
what: Not a reduce but an iterate_until(step, is_finished, state0) driver (a scan when the trace is kept); the step is a single attempt that accepts or rejects and adjusts μ; the LM step is separated from the model, which supplies Φ, gradient and exact Hessian, giving a generic LM_step(model, state).

quote: Luthier entonces da las invariantes para cada etapa. Y luego lo que se puede hacer es comparar el MAP_... de python con un MAP_ sintetico en luthier ensamblando las steps. De este modo se testea y documenta en un solo paso.
what: Make the step functions accessible to Luthier, have Luthier give the invariants for each stage, and compare the Python MAP with a synthetic MAP assembled in Luthier from the steps, testing and documenting in a single step.

quote: El `.lut` que ensambla el MAP pasa a ser la especificación legible del algoritmo, y las invariantes de cada etapa su contrato.
what: The per-stage invariants test the components; the Python-vs-Luthier comparison tests only the assembly (and only if the Luthier assembly is independent), and being deterministic it can be exact step by step; the .lut assembling the MAP becomes the legible specification of the algorithm.

quote: yo partiria de cero con Luthier, justamente quiero ir liviano con lo imprescindible. Mi idea es generar una forma de trabajo para que despues escale, pero primero tenemos que hacer todos los pasos detalladamente.
what: Start from zero in Luthier with only the indispensable, generating a way of working that later scales but doing every step in detail first; begin with the likelihood and the sampler.

open: what to call the relation ("adjoint" or otherwise).
quote: declarar que la likelihood de las posiciones respecto de las distancias dado el error esperado tiene como adjoint (o veremos como llamarlo) a un sampler de distancias dadas las posiciones y error esperado). aqui hay un tema y es que esta relacion vale para la likelihood completa, sospecho que para la profile likelihood no vale.
what: Define the score expectation/variance test generically for a generic likelihood and sampler, then declare that the likelihood of positions given distances and expected error has as its adjoint a sampler of distances given positions and expected error; he suspects the relation holds for the complete likelihood but not the profiled one.

open: the naming of the relation is left to Luciano.
quote: **Propuesta: la perfilada no tiene sampler propio.** Se testea reduciéndola a la completa, con una identidad determinista que vale para cada y
what: The profiled likelihood is not a density of y (it does not integrate to one); its second identity fails by a factor K/(K−2); so it has no own sampler and is tested by a deterministic identity reducing it to the complete likelihood. The model also questions the name "adjoint" and proposes `is_density_of(likelihood, sampler)`.

quote: yo lo pensaba como adjoint functor de CT
what: Luciano was thinking of the sampler-likelihood relation as an adjoint functor of category theory.

quote: lo que el test de Bartlett verifica es la normalización, ∫ L(y; θ) dy = 1 para todo θ. En categorías de Markov esa es justamente la axioma que define un morfismo
what: Not adjoint functors but adjoint operators: sampler and likelihood are one Markov kernel read two ways; the push-forward (Perron-Frobenius) and pull-back (Koopman) operators are linear-algebra adjoints; the Bartlett test verifies normalization, the axiom that defines a morphism of Markov categories, which the profiled likelihood fails because it is not a kernel.

quote: definir is_density_of diciendo que eso implica las identidades que dijimos, con eso testeamos sampler y loglikelihood completa. luego necesitamos una propiedad que una loglikelihood completa con profiled. esta segunda propiedad se da para las likelihoods \"gausianas\" donde perfilamos el sigma .
what: Define `is_density_of` as implying the stated identities to test sampler and complete log-likelihood, then add a property linking the complete log-likelihood with the profiled one, which holds for "gaussian" likelihoods where σ is profiled; express the first in Luthier.

quote: no entendiste un carajo. Lee mi paper en /home/lmoffatt/Code/macro_dr/macro_dr/papers/1_method/docs/
what: Luciano rejects the model's finite-difference/z-score proposal and points to his paper; the model then restates (turn 82) that in his framework the likelihood reports its own Fisher information H, and the diagnostic measures a matrix (bias b and distortion C, the sandwich) rather than passing or failing a threshold.

quote: Declarar que la likelihood es la densidad del sampler es declarar b = 0 y C = I dentro del piso.
what: The likelihood is an object reporting its Fisher information H; the diagnostic compares reported H against delivered J over true-process data, yielding the displacement b = H⁻¹E[S] and distortion C = H^(−1/2) J H^(−1/2) as measured quantities; declaring the likelihood is the sampler's density is declaring b = 0 and C = I within a sampling floor; the profiled likelihood is a member with m = K/(K−2), not a failure.

quote: No, hagamos al reves. Primero pensemos el lut
what: Design the .lut first, before the Python function definitions.

quote: Las likelihoods gaussianas son una construcción, no un caso. ... Eso da un constructor, y la perfilada es otro constructor sobre el mismo modelo
what: Organize Luthier around three concepts: sampler and likelihood as two readings of one kernel (likelihood a record with loglik, score, info); gaussian likelihoods as a construction with constructors `gaussian` and `profiled` over a `GaussianModel`; and the diagnostic as a measurement over an ensemble with b and C defined by their property.

quote: gaussian y profiled justamente deben escribirse tanto como extern como nativas de luthier. Luego las comparamos como test. Ese seria el paradigma. En luthier es lento y conceptual y lo comparo con python que es relativamente rapido y pragmatico, luego si quiero mas velocidad quizas lo implemente en C++.
what: The paradigm: each concept (gaussian, profiled) is written twice, native in Luthier and extern in Python, and the test is that they agree; Luthier is slow and conceptual, Python relatively fast and pragmatic, and C++ later if more speed is wanted.

quote: `density.lut`: las definiciones nativas ... `density_fast.lut`: los mismos nombres, todos `extern` a numpy. ... `density_agree.lut`: una ley por función ... y los `test`.
what: Organize by modules with the same names: a native `density.lut` (reference), a `density_fast.lut` all extern to numpy, and a `density_agree.lut` with one agreement law per function plus the tests; b and distortion defined in Luthier by their property (H b = E[S], H Σ H = J) rather than by construction.

quote: en una subsecuente version hariamos la version nativa del subespacio y autovalores porque justamente son altamente conceptuales.
what: Defer the native version of the retained subspace and eigenvalues to a later version precisely because they are highly conceptual.

quote: creo que Luthier podria usar algo mas rapido que listas y recursion quizas asi tenemos mas millage, sino si todo es list(a, list(b,list(c))) nos pegamos un tiro.
what: Luthier should use something faster than lists and recursion for more mileage; nesting everything as list(a, list(b, list(c))) is untenable.

quote: Mi recomendación es el primitivo de arreglo ... Los primitivos ... no tienen versión nativa; se certifican como en `algebra.lut`, por sus leyes algebraicas con generadores

what: Archive at minimum all sonolocalization .lut files; at most the Python interpreter too, but that is deferred since he does not look at it much and it can be done later once the functionality exists.

quote: **Tolerancias.** `tolOf n = 8 · n · eps`. ... **`==` no decide sobre arreglos.** Comparar es `approxR`, `approxVec` o `approxMat`
what: Two decisions taken in the arrays work: tolerance `tolOf n = 8·n·eps` scaling by the product of norms where the two sides of a law can cancel, with the 8 a named slack declared once; and `==` does not decide over arrays, comparison being `approxR/approxVec/approxMat`.

quote: El evaluador de Luthier reduce por sustitución: en cada beta hace `subst(head.body, b)`, que copia el cuerpo entero reemplazando la variable ... así que el costo por paso crece con n y el total es cuadrático o peor.
what: Luthier's evaluator reduces by substitution, copying the whole body on each beta and match, so the cost per recursion step grows with the term size, which is quadratic or worse on lists.

quote: Un evaluador con entornos es la alternativa estándar. En lugar de sustituir, una lambda se evalúa a una clausura: el cuerpo sin tocar más un entorno que dice qué vale cada variable.
what: An evaluator with environments (closures plus normalization by evaluation to recover normal forms as terms) as the standard alternative, bounded as a core rewrite that must preserve holes, externs, match, subtypes, fuel and the 43 tests.

quote: el evaluador con entornos estaria en la wish list urgente. Vamos con la alternativa B

what: Declare `Vec : U := extern python` and instantiate `Ring Vec` with the members (+, *, zero) bound to extern Python implementations.

what: A class over a carrier needs the carrier's notion of equality, which for floats is an approximation with tolerance; so `Ring A` should carry `eq : A -> A -> Bool` as a member (a setoid), letting the same Ring serve integers, reals and arrays.

quote: Lo que vos querés es el literal con nombres, que es mejor: independiente del orden y legible.
what: A record literal with named fields, `{ add := ..., mul := ... }`, checked field by field by name against the dependent product of the type, better than the positional tuple.

quote: estaria bueno usar los operadores + , * , ^ etc no? o se prestaria a confusion por la suma de tipos?
what: Would it be good to use the operators +, *, ^ for the class members, or does it risk confusion with the sum of types?

quote: en `A * B` los operandos son tipos (están en `U`), en `x * y` son valores; el elaborador sabe cuál es cuál porque chequea bidireccionalmente y conoce el tipo de cada operando.
what: The confusion between the sum of types and the sum of values is not real for the checker, because bidirectional elaboration knows whether operands are types (in `U`) or values.

open: `^` left out for now, defined by recursion over `*`.
quote: Lo que sí hace falta es resolución por tipo, o sea clases de tipos de verdad.
what: Using operators for class members needs real type classes: members named by the operator, instances registered per carrier and class, and resolution in the elaborator by the operand types; heterogeneous operators (c·v as scale) resolved by (operator, left type, right type).

quote: entonces podemos definir los cuerpos de reales, ring de enteros, vector fields de vectores y matrices etc.
what: With that in place, define the ring of reals, ring of integers, vector fields of vectors and matrices, etc.

open: Honesties to declare: the inverse lives in `{ x : R | x /= 0.0 }` and float associativity holds only within rounding.
quote: la misma `Ring` certificada sobre `Int` con `==` exacto y sobre `R` con `approx` muestra que el esquema está bien armado.
what: `Ring Int` with exact `==` as the control instance: if the laws pass with `==` and with `approx` depending on the carrier, equality by class works; define only the hierarchy that `density.lut` uses.

quote: si tenemos Innerproduct que es una measure field? busquemos los conceptos matematicos que corresponden.
what: If there is InnerProduct, is it a measure field? Find the matching mathematical concepts.

quote: el producto interno no es un accidente de la implementación: es el concepto que une el álgebra lineal con la estadística.
what: A bottom-up stack of mathematical concepts as types: measurable space and measure, density as Radon-Nikodym derivative, Markov kernel (the single object behind sampler and likelihood), expectation as positive linear functional, and inner product entering twice (Fisher metric on Θ, precision on Y).

quote: la información de Fisher es la matriz de Gram de los scores ... la información es el producto interno de `L²(P_θ)` restringido al espacio tangente del modelo.
what: Fisher information is the inner product of L²(P_θ) restricted to the model's tangent space: the Gram matrix of the scores, making Θ a Riemannian manifold (Rao-Amari information geometry).

quote: el modelo gaussiano como aplicación entre espacios con producto interno. ... Todo lo del punto 5 se deriva de ahí ... Esa es la clase que `density.lut` tendría que definir, y de la que `gaussian` y `profiled` son construcciones.
what: The structure to name is the gaussian model as a map `h : Θ → Y` between inner-product spaces, from which likelihood, score, information and Levenberg-Marquardt (Gauss-Newton in the pullback metric) all derive; this is the class `density.lut` should define.

quote: con la vision de que tratamos de introducir los tipos con propiedades, reescribamos todo lut
what: With the vision of introducing types with properties, rewrite the whole `.lut` layer.

quote: la likelihood perfilada sí cumple las identidades del paper. Yo había dicho que fallaba por un factor K/(K−2).
what: The model corrects its earlier claim: the profiled likelihood does satisfy the paper's identities; the K/(K−2) factor compares against minus the expected Hessian, while the paper compares against the information the likelihood reports; it is exact at the true parameter but the profiled is not a density (does not integrate to one).

quote: `shift t (zeros d)` es t.
what: `shift` lacks laws of its own; it should satisfy `shift t (zeros d)` is t, and that moving by `scale ε v` changes ℓ to first order as ε times the directional derivative.

quote: En términos de geometría, `shift` es la retracción de una variedad: el mapa que lleva un vector tangente a un punto vecino.
what: `shift t v` moves parameter t in direction v, distinguishing the parameter space `Theta` from the tangent space `Vec` where score, information and directions live; it is the retraction of a manifold, letting `ScoreIsGradient` hold for any `Theta`.

quote: si, agregala.
what: Add the `ShiftByZero` law.

quote: `Theta` no tiene igualdad propia, así que la ley la lee a través de lo que la likelihood ve.
what: Since `Theta` is generic and has no equality of its own, the law reads it through what the likelihood sees: it compares ℓ(y, shift t 0) with ℓ(y, t) exactly.

quote: se podria hace luthier puro, definiendo Vec como una\"clase\" que tiene una serie de accesors y inpectors (length at etc). Luego tendriamos probability_python.lut donde conectamos todas las estructuras con sus implementaciones.
what: Since `probability.lut` has almost no externs, make Luthier pure by defining `Vec` as a "class" with accessors and inspectors, and have a `probability_python.lut` that connects the structures to their implementations.

quote: `array.lut` declara los portadores y las operaciones sin cuerpo ... `array_python.lut` importa la interfaz y llena cada hueco con su extern ... `probability.lut` importa solo la interfaz y queda Luthier puro.
what: Two ways to split interface from implementation: module holes (a file declares carriers and operations without body, a linking file fills each hole with its extern) or the implementation as an argument (an ML functor); recommends holes now, the argument form when two implementations must coexist in one program.

quote: El patron seria que las puras son como las clases virtuales de C++, no tienen implementacion. Luego se las implementa en python.
what: The pattern: the pure files are like C++ pure virtual classes, no implementation, then implemented in Python.

quote: **Leyes:** el contrato que la implementación tiene que cumplir. Una clase virtual de C++ no tiene esto. Ahí el contrato vive en la documentación y nadie lo verifica.
what: Two matices that make the pattern better than a virtual class: pure files also hold concrete definitions built on the leaves (valid for any implementation) and laws that are a verified contract, which a C++ virtual class lacks; linking is at program-assembly time, fixing one implementation for the whole program.

quote: Es la capa del entorno, igual que `R` mismo, que el intérprete llena. Separarla implicaría que todo programa de Luthier, ejemplos incluidos, importe una vinculación para tener números.
what: `real.lut` keeps its externs (exp, log, sqrt, cbrt) as the environment layer, like `R` itself that the interpreter fills, so that every Luthier program need not import a linking file to have numbers.

open: Luciano does not know how to express it.
quote: en realidad el prior y el posterior son lo mismo dependen de donde esta situado el \"cursosr\". No se como expresariamos eso?
what: Don't restrict posterior to such a specific case; prior and posterior are the same thing, depending on where the "cursor" sits.

quote: No hay dos conceptos, prior y posterior. Hay uno solo, el estado de conocimiento sobre θ, y una operación que lo actualiza con datos.
what: Formalize it as a single `Belief Theta` with an `Update` operation; the prior is `after u b []`, the posterior `after u b ys`, the cursor being the position in the data sequence; with four implementation-independent laws (composition, exchangeability, evidence chain, calibration).

open: Requires the Laplace update to work in the subspace where precision is non-null.
quote: Una precisión con autovalores nulos es una creencia impropia, \"nada se sabe en esta dirección\". El prior de partida puede tener precisión cero en las direcciones rígidas
what: The information form also resolves the gauge: a precision with null eigenvalues is an improper belief ("nothing known in this direction"), so rigid directions stay at precision zero without inventing tiny σ or removing coordinates.

quote: el MAP deja de ser un caso aparte: es cómo se implementa la actualización de una creencia gaussiana.
what: A gaussian belief in information form is not closed under exact update; the Laplace update closes it, the new mean being the MAP (via Levenberg-Marquardt) and the new precision minus the Hessian at the MAP, so the MAP stops being a separate case.

quote: Si arma belief.lut (es puro no?)
what: Build `belief.lut`, confirming it is pure.

quote: **`BeliefFamily`:** un tipo de estados de conocimiento sobre θ, con cuatro operaciones. Actualizar por un dato, el log predictivo de ese dato, sortear un θ, y decidir si dos creencias dicen lo mismo.
what: `BeliefFamily`: a type of states of knowledge about θ with four operations (update by a datum, log-predictive of that datum, draw a θ, decide if two beliefs agree), with the discrete belief as exact Bayes reference and the gaussian belief in information form.

quote: Evaluar por sustitución obliga a forzar los argumentos. Un argumento usado varias veces se recalcula en cada uso.
what: Evaluating by substitution recomputes a multiply-used argument on each use; a single draw took 12 s versus 0.6 s when forced once with `match`, which is a further argument for the environment evaluator.

quote: Agregué `--fuel` al CLI de Luthier. El límite de 200 000 pasos por reducción estaba fijo en el código ... y no debería estar cableado.
what: Added `--fuel` to the Luthier CLI because the 200 000-step reduction limit was hard-coded, and it is a run parameter that should not be wired in.

quote: hagamos el evaluador con entornos por favor, que es la idea de Luthier que las cosas se calculan usa sola vez y los conceptos serian unicos
what: Build the environment evaluator, framed as the Luthier idea that things are computed only once and concepts would be unique.

quote: es un poco como pasar por referencia en c++?
what: Is this a bit like passing by reference in C++?

quote: Cada argumento y cada constante se calculan una sola vez, y todo corre entre 5 y 10 veces más rápido.
what: The environment evaluator is working: each argument and constant computed once (lazy memoized closures), tail calls in a loop, 5-10× faster; the checker keeps the substitution evaluator for normalizing types (small terms, possibly free variables), with fallback when the new one can't handle something.

quote: Propongo dejar la información, y agregar el Hessiano observado a `Likelihood` como un miembro opcional para cuando se quiera comparar.
what: For the new precision, choose between the information reported at the MAP or the observed Hessian; proposes keeping the reported information (matching the paper's H) and adding the observed Hessian to `Likelihood` as an optional member for comparison.

quote: si, acepto tu propuesta
what: Accepts the proposal to keep the reported information.

quote: la información reportada es la curvatura esperada bajo el modelo, y el Hessiano observado es la curvatura de los datos que tenés.
what: The reported information is the expected curvature under the model, the observed Hessian the curvature of the data you have; at the MAP they differ by a term weighing 0.1% to 1% in the positions.

quote: **Las leyes reciben la implementación como argumento.** Así van a certificar después el paso de Python sin cambios
what: `optimization.lut` as pure: `Objective` (value, gradient, step matrix), `LMState`, `lmStep`, `finished` with its reason, `minimize` driver and `lmMaximizer`, with laws (StepRule, DescentDirection, Certified, Converges) receiving the implementation as argument so they later certify the Python step unchanged.

open: Luciano's choice between tolerance and convergence law; model recommends the second.
quote: **Como ley de convergencia.** El apartamiento tiene que achicarse con el ruido: medido a σ, σ/2 y σ/4, cada vez debe caer por lo menos al orden esperado... Sin umbral arbitrario, y separa lo estructural de la aproximación: un error de código no se achica con σ.
what: Writing the Laplace-update laws as a law of convergence, where the departure must shrink with the noise at the expected order, rather than with a chosen tolerance threshold.

quote: si, con la 2
what: Takes the convergence-law option.

quote: es realmente diagnostico este test?
what: Asks whether the test actually diagnoses anything.

quote: Un test es diagnóstico si una actualización equivocada falla... Cualquier aproximación consistente se anula al achicar σ, incluso una mala, así que la ley confirma un orden pero no la corrección a σ finito.
what: A test is diagnostic only if a wrong update fails it; a consistent approximation, even a bad one, vanishes as σ shrinks, so a convergence law confirms an order but not correctness at finite σ. Hence negative controls are needed.

quote: las leyes de convergencia no agregan corrección, solo una medida de la calidad de la aproximación.
what: The convergence laws are removed as tests: they add no correctness, only a measure of how far Laplace departs from exact Bayes; the Laplace update is already covered by diagnostic tests (MAP certificate, `IsDensityOf`).

quote: la calidad de la covergencia es una propiedad de la funcion que estamos optimizando no del algoritmo no? O sea esto es para testear el algoritmo no la funcion en particular o me equivoco?
what: Distinguishes that convergence quality belongs to the function being optimized, so such a test would test the algorithm, not the particular function.

quote: Hay dos convergencias distintas, y en la conversación las mezclé bajo la misma palabra.
what: Separates the optimizer's convergence (a property of the algorithm) from the convergence of the Laplace laws (a property of the approximation applied to this function); the order is generic to Laplace, but where the asymptotic regime begins is function-specific (Bates-Watts curvature).

open: whether an IO monad is needed now; model answers (turn 181) that it is not.
quote: input output es un lugar para bugs. Entonces tenemos que conceptualizar la IO monad en luthier? Necesitamos el par read write que acoplados tienen la invariante que si read->write-> read == read y otras cosas.
what: Luthierize the input/output of sonolocalización because IO is a place for bugs; conceptualize an IO monad in Luthier, a coupled read/write pair with the invariant that read→write→read equals read, and conceptualize dataframes in Luthier.

quote: En la jerga de óptica esto es un *prism*, una isomorfía parcial. Ya tenemos `Iso` en `algebra.lut`, y el códec sería su versión parcial.
what: Separate the trivial effect (an extern with no laws) from the format, a pure codec with two laws, `parse (render t) == ok t` and `parse ∘ render ∘ parse == parse`; the codec is a partial isomorphism, a prism, the partial version of the existing `Iso`.

quote: un script de python convierta a distancias en un distancias_ready para el MAP y que ese script no se hasta que punto vale la pena luthierizarlo. La idea es que los esquemas luthier sean muy re-utilizables.
what: A Python script should convert distances into a `distancias_ready` for the MAP, and it is doubtful that script is worth luthierizing; the Luthier schemas should be highly reusable, not the throwaway per-experiment conversion.

quote: Lo reutilizable no es la conversión: es el formato al que toda conversión tiene que llegar." / "Es validar en la frontera: la lógica descartable queda libre, y el punto donde entra al sistema está bajo contrato.
what: What is reusable is not the conversion but the format every conversion must reach; the per-experiment Python conversion stays outside Luthier, its only contract being that its output passes the schema, validated at the frontier.

quote: vamos a correr cosas en luthier o solo testear? me parece que podemos hacer ambos como una forma de volver legible un proyecto escrito en python.
what: Luthier should both run and test, as a way to make a project written in Python legible.

quote: un programa que corre no puede divergir de su documentación, porque es la documentación." / "lo que itera sobre datos es hoja, lo que itera sobre conceptos es composición.
what: A three-level cut (leaves in Python, composition in Luthier, orchestration); a program that runs cannot diverge from its documentation because it is the documentation; the design rule is that what iterates over data is a leaf and what iterates over concepts is composition.

quote: no seria hacer luthier miexperimento.lut mejor que python miexperimento.py?
what: Questions why orchestration stays in Python; proposes `luthier miexperimento.lut` instead of `python miexperimento.py`.

quote: En Luthier eso es un hueco: `tapeSigma : R` declarado sin cuerpo, y `luthier run miexperimento.lut --set tapeSigma=0.03`. El valor queda en el certificado junto con los hashes
what: A criterion is a hole, a declaration without a body, filled from the command line with `--set` and recorded in the certificate with the hashes; effects become externs and a `luthier run` command evaluates a main definition with effects.

quote: hacemos el test con luthier de MAP, pero despues usamos MAP para el experimento no?
what: Asks whether the MAP is tested with Luthier but then used for the experiment.

quote: El MAP nativo de Luthier es la definición: con él se certifica el de Python, que coincide paso a paso y corre cien veces más rápido. Una vez certificado, el experimento usa el de Python.
what: The native Luthier MAP is the definition that certifies the Python one, which matches step by step and runs a hundred times faster; once certified, the experiment uses the Python one, and running the native on real data was misusing the definition as an implementation.

quote: Todas las corridas convergían mucho antes de las 200 iteraciones, así que esa rama nunca se ejercitaba. Por eso agregué la ley con presupuestos de 1 a 5 iteraciones, y con ella el control falla. Era un hueco real de la certificación
what: A negative control (checking the iteration budget before convergence) initially passed because every run converged well before the limit, so that branch was never exercised; adding a law with small budgets closed a real gap in the certification.

quote: Cloud me genera todo, código de Luthier, y qué sé yo, pero para mí eso no es código, es como que no está cumpliendo con las normativas reales de Luthier, o quizás sí, eso es lo que yo no entiendo
what: What Claude generates as Luthier code feels to him like not-code, as if it fails to meet Luthier's real norms, and he is unsure whether it does or not.

quote: **El modelo Typeclass / Concept / Teoría de Modelos:** Un concepto (o teoría matemática) es un contrato abstracto abierto ... Una implementación concreta (ej. Pandas DataFrame) es simplemente un **modelo** que satisface esa teoría.
what: Gives a theoretical correlate to Luciano's two ways: the C++ closed model tightly couples representation to operations; the typeclass/theory-of-models model is an open contract (declares types, operations, axioms) that a concrete implementation satisfies as a model.

quote: vos declaras el tipo lo declaras y después lo definís ... es universal listo pero no está definido ... sería como una especie de clase pura que no se puede instanciar ... no podés declarar, por ejemplo, que ... una variable es una tabla hasta que vos no hayas ... definido que es una tabla
what: A type can be declared (universal) before it is defined; while only declared it is like a pure class that cannot be instantiated or used, e.g. you cannot declare a variable is a Table until Table is defined with its construction and functions.

quote: yo ahora construyo una tabla ... entonces tengo la garantía de que yo puedo acceder a toda una serie de, como se dice, de métodos, que eso es básicamente estamos descubriendo la programación de objetos ... casero
what: Declaring that something is of a type should already guarantee a series of methods/properties; building a Table gives the guarantee you can use all its methods, which he recognizes is rediscovering object-oriented programming.

quote: yo ponen que tenga operaciones que sean derivadas ... sus invariantes van a estar definidas por otras operaciones. esas operaciones tienen que ya estar definidas. Si no están definidas, no, es inválido
what: An operation whose invariants are defined in terms of other operations requires those operations to already be defined; otherwise it is invalid.

quote: ahora quiero hacer un luthier efectivo que haga algo, por ejemplo, que vos puedas definir en leyes, por ejemplo, que una función sea la inversa de otra ... primero conviene, sí, testear lo mínimo posible y después ir avanzando
what: He wants an effective Luthier that does something (e.g. declare in laws that one function is the inverse of another) without defining the invariants of every element, testing the minimum first and advancing from there.

quote: con una especie de sintaxis libre que vos vas definiendo distintas invariantes, así alegremente, y después decís, bueno, ahora yo quiero tal y tal asegurarlas ... Me parece que esa es la lógica que está siguiendo ahora Luthier ... sirve para lo que sería hacer test porque vos testeas cosas alegremente todas independientes una de la otra
what: A loose free syntax where you declare various invariants freely and then say which ones you want to ensure; he thinks this is the logic current Luthier (without its Claude) follows, and it is expressive and fine for writing tests independently of each other.

quote: muchas funciones y tipos van en conjunto ... como los objetos matemáticos, como el grupo ... si vos tenés un objeto matemático, está definido todo junto. O sea, vos no podés definir una parte sola del objeto matemático
what: Many functions and types belong together as a single mathematical object (group, monoid); you cannot define one part alone, the object is defined whole.

quote: las operaciones son en este mundo ideal, sin errores, y después vos las aproximás ... las leyes no se van a hacer precisas, sino que van a tener una cierta garantía. El tema es que calcular esa garantía puede ser más complejo que calcular el valor en sí ... Vos lo podés reducir en una cuestión de optimización
what: Operations live in an ideal error-free world and are approximated in reality (reals by floating point); laws hold not exactly but with a precision guarantee, and the tradeoff between guarantee and reachable values becomes an optimization problem.

quote: yo tengo que definir ese invariante para su vez, tengo que definir para el resto, está definiendo dos veces, o sea que en realidad, digamos, la invariante sería para el par
what: An invariant like "sum is the inverse of subtraction" would otherwise be defined twice, once per function; instead the invariant belongs to the pair.

quote: El nudo en el que estás no es de sintaxis, sino de **semántica de tipos**. Claude tiende a generar código de "Luthier" inventando sintaxis ad-hoc o cayendo en *property-based testing* tradicional ... porque todavía no tiene anclada la semántica formal del lenguaje.
what: The difficulty is one of type semantics, not syntax; Claude invents ad-hoc syntax or falls into traditional property-based testing because it lacks the formal semantics anchored.

quote: las leyes son ecuaciones sobre la signatura conjunta, no definiciones operacionales recursivas ... La teoría `TableModel` empaqueta el grafo cíclico de relaciones en una sola unidad semántica.
what: The circularity resolves because laws are equations over the joint signature, not recursive operational definitions; a theory packages the cyclic graph of relations into one semantic unit where no function owns another.

open: Whether there can be mathematical objects without equality; he notes reals use equivalence rather than equality and leaves it unresolved.
quote: la idea siempre es hacer lo más general posible ... lo único que necesitas probablemente son los operadores lógicos y posiblemente sí, bueno, igualdad ... en fondo para teoría de categorías necesitas igualdad
what: Aim for the most general definition, specializing no more than needed; probably only logical operators and equality are required, as category theory needs only equality of arrows and uniqueness.

quote: un objeto matemático no es un tipo de datos; es una signatura algebraica con leyes acopladas.
what: Restates as a key conclusion that a mathematical object is an algebraic signature with coupled laws, not a data type.

quote: si vos tenés una circularidad ... la circularidad de las invariantes, que vos tenés dos funciones que vos necesitás una para probar la otra ... ahí vos necesitás crearla juntas y ahí estás generando un objeto. O sea, los objetos son ... grafos cíclicos ... en su definición
what: Circularity of invariants (two functions each needed to prove the other) forces them to be created together, which is what generates an object; objects are cyclic graphs in their definition.

quote: vos podés tener objetos matemáticos que son, digamos, puros en el sentido de que surgen de la nada y otros que se basan en otros objetos, son derivados
what: Some mathematical objects are pure (arise from nothing, like the set object Z), others are derived, built on other objects (groups over Set or over other objects).

quote: son dos tipos serían reales incluyendo el cero o reales excluyendo el cero ... al decir que vos te estás diciendo que algo es de un tipo vos ya estás garantizando toda una serie de ... cosas
what: Division by zero motivates distinguishing two types: reals including zero and reals excluding zero, so that declaring the type already guarantees the operation is defined.

quote: una table, si la vamos a definir, digamos, con teoría y categoría ... es un vector de la suma de vectores de ... determinado largo fijo eso es una tabla estructuralmente ... el vector ya tiene el operador índice ... aplicando dos veces el operador entonces llegas a seleccionar columna y row
what: A table can be defined constructively in category-theory terms as a vector of sums of vectors of fixed length, each column returning a variant (sum of possible types); from the vector's index operator everything else (row/column selection) follows.

open: Offered to work out the concrete grammar of a minimal case (InversePair or Table); Luciano has not answered.
quote: **`spec` (o `concept`)** ... **`refinement` (Subtipado por predicado)** ... restringiendo un tipo existente mediante una precondición explícita ... **`instance` (o `model`)** ... aportando las garantías (sean de verificación formal estática o de testing con tolerancia numérica $\varepsilon$ para flotantes).
what: Proposes structuring Luthier's grammar in three constructs: spec/concept (abstract interface and joint laws), refinement (predicate subtyping, e.g. reals without zero), and instance/model (mapping a real type to the spec and supplying guarantees, static or with tolerance ε for floats).

quote: **El Tipo Portador (*Carrier Type*)** ... **Las Operaciones (Morfismos/Signatura)** ... **Las Leyes (Invariantes / Ecuaciones)** ... la invariante no pertenece a la función, sino al **sistema algebraico** que las engloba.
what: Separate three levels: the carrier type (raw data), the operations (morphisms/signature), and the laws (invariants/equations linking the operations); a law over more than one function belongs to the algebraic system, not the function.

quote: Una es, yo defino a table junto con todas las funciones que operan sobre table, un poco al estilo objetos ... La otra ... yo defino table como un tipo así como simplemente un puntero al vacío después defino todas las funciones ... y después defino ... los constraints ... el único tema es que es como una clase abierta
what: Two ways to define Table: closed, C++-object style (type with its list of functions and their invariants all together), or open, as a void pointer plus separately defined functions and constraints; the same information, but the open one lacks a block end that guarantees it is a Table.

quote: un poco la idea de Luthier es que uno pueda escribir, digamos, que las clases, los tipos, queden definidos por sus, ¿cómo se llama? Invariantes, ¿no? O sea, todos los invariantes que tienen que tener los tipos, incluyendo las funciones
what: The core idea of Luthier: types, including functions, are defined by the invariants they must have.

quote: Dividir por cero te lleva a pensar en dos tipos distintos: reales con el cero y reales sin el cero.
what: Model summarizing Luciano's audio: division by zero leads to thinking of two distinct types, reals with zero and reals without it.

quote: El codec ya está en el estilo cerrado que pedís.
what: Model's own diagnosis: `LawfulCodec` already is the closed style requested (parse and render joined with their four laws), so the grammar already has the mechanism; what is missing is applying it to Table.

quote: Table se define junto con sus operaciones esenciales y sus invariantes, en un solo bloque. Hasta que el bloque no se cierra, Table no existe y no se puede usar.
what: Model summarizing Luciano's audio of 10:28: a type can be defined closed (a single block with its operations and invariants, unusable until closed) or open (empty type, loose functions, restrictions added later).

quote: Una ley que liga dos funciones (la suma es la inversa de la resta) le pertenece al par, no a cada función por separado.
what: Model summarizing Luciano's audio: a law tying two functions belongs to the pair, not to each function alone.

quote: Al bajar a floats, cada ley pasa a valer con una garantía de precisión, y calcular esa garantía puede costar más que calcular el valor.
what: Model summarizing Luciano's audio: operations live in an ideal error-free world; descending to floats each law holds with a precision guarantee, which can cost more to compute than the value itself.
